faq.a: Snow is made of ice crystals that grew in clouds from water vapour, often in six-sided shapes. Fresh snow is mostly air trapped between those crystals.
asks: What is a snowflake made of?

faq.a: Scattering is when light bounces off in many different directions instead of going straight through. Snow, clouds and milk scatter light so much that they look white.
asks: Why do some things scatter light?

faq.q: Why does snow look blue in deep holes?
faq.a: Ice absorbs a tiny bit more red light than blue. Light that travels deep into snow loses some red on the way, so the inside of a hole or a thick glacier glows blue.
For the same reason as snow: crushing makes many small pieces with lots of surfaces, and each surface scatters light. All colours together come back as white.
asks: Why is salt white but rock salt clear?

faq.q: Why does snow make it so bright outside?
faq.a: Fresh snow reflects up to about 90 percent of the sunlight that hits it. That is why snowy days are dazzling and skiers wear sunglasses.

facts: Fresh snow can reflect up to about 90 percent of sunlight.
Ice absorbs slightly more red light than blue, which is why glacier ice and deep snow holes look blue.

quiz.say: Which of these is white for the same reason as snow?
quiz.show: White for the same reason as snow:
quiz.why: Crushed ice has many small surfaces that scatter all colours of light equally, so it looks white like snow.

wrong.1: A ruby is red because it absorbs some colours and lets red through.
wrong.2: A leaf is green because chlorophyll absorbs red and blue light.
